records.subject: All-flexible quasi-solid-state thermogalvanic cells
records.object: Maximum power density: 4.05 mW m−2 K−2
records.quote: Herein, we present novel strategies for developing high-performance all-flexible QTCs using both metallized fibril-based textile electrodes with extremely large surface area, (specifically Ni textiles), and structure-breaking salts for hydrogel electrolytes.
context_quotes: The electrodes are oxidized to create Ni and Ni oxide heterostructures, forming numerous O vacancy defects that enhance redox reactions.
Meanwhile, the structure-breaking salts facilitate redox reactions and improve ion diffusion by disrupting water structures in the hydrogel electrolyte.

These advancements significantly enhance the performance of the QTCs without the need for precious-metal electrodes, achieving a remarkable maximum power density of 4.05 mW m-2 K-2 and a record-high effective cell conductivity of 17.3 S m-1, compared to previously reported QTCs.
records.conditions: Compared with previously reported QTCs; without precious-metal electrodes
